evals.name: rich-request-generate
evals.prompt: I need a prompt I can paste into Gemini that writes our sprint retro summary. It goes out to the eng leadership staff meeting, needs to stay under 300 words, and should have three sections: what shipped, what slipped, what we're changing next sprint. I've got last sprint's retro doc that came out well and I can paste it in as an example of the format. Nobody wants to read hedging language so it should be blunt about what slipped.
evals.expected_output: A copy-pasteable TCREI prompt block ([TASK]/[CONTEXT]/[REFERENCES] or XML equivalent) with an action verb + specific persona + named output format in Task, the audience/word limit/three sections/blunt tone in Context, and a slot for the user's prior retro doc in References. No unnecessary interview — audience, constraints, and ground truth were all supplied.
evals.trap: Agent writes the retro summary itself instead of a prompt, or emits a prompt buried in paragraphs of explanation, or drops the 300-word limit and the three named sections.
assertions: The response contains a prompt block delimited by bracket headers ([TASK]/[CONTEXT]/[REFERENCES]) or the XML equivalent (<task>/<context>/<references>)
The Task section names an action verb, a domain-specific persona (not 'helpful assistant', 'AI assistant', or a bare 'expert'), and a named output format
The Context section carries both the 300-word limit and all three named sections (what shipped / what slipped / what we're changing next sprint)
The Context section names eng leadership as the audience and expresses the blunt-about-slippage requirement as an affirmative directive rather than only as a 'do not hedge' prohibition
The References section provides a paste slot for the user's own prior retro doc and does not contain a fabricated example retro
The response is the prompt block plus at most two sentences of framing — no component-by-component breakdown of the choices
The response asks no clarifying questions, since audience, constraints, and ground truth were all supplied in the request
The response does not itself contain a written sprint retro summary

evals.name: thin-request-interview
evals.prompt: make me a prompt for writing release notes
evals.expected_output: A short batch of targeted questions closing the audience / constraints / ground-truth gaps (e.g. who reads them, is there a past release note to match, any length or format requirement), each with a suggested default so the user can confirm rather than compose. Should not dump a generic prompt as if the request were fully specified.
evals.trap: Agent immediately produces a generic release-notes prompt with invented audience and format, presenting guesses as if they were requirements.
assertions: The response asks two or three questions, delivered together in one turn rather than one at a time

At least two of the questions map onto distinct un-inventable fields: audience, hard constraints (length / required sections / format), and ground truth (an existing release note or style guide to match)
Every question carries a concrete suggested default or proposed answer, so the user can confirm rather than compose
The response does not emit a finished prompt block presented as ready to paste — or, if it offers a provisional draft, every invented specific in it is marked inline as an assumption
The response does not ask about anything inferable from the answers (tone, persona, section headings) — those are inferred, not interviewed
The response does not itself write release notes

evals.name: improve-existing-prompt
evals.prompt: This prompt keeps giving me walls of text and I don't know why. Can you fix it? --- 'You are a helpful assistant. Review the customer support ticket and give a good summary. Don't be too long. Try not to miss anything important.'
evals.expected_output: A revised prompt block that replaces the generic persona with a specific one, converts 'good'/'not too long'/'not miss anything' into measurable constraints (word or sentence count, named sections/fields), flips the negative constraints to affirmative directives, and notes the missing References component. Followed by a brief list of what changed and why.
evals.trap: Agent adds more instructions and a generic 'expert' role without quantifying the vague terms, leaving 'don't be too long' as an unenforceable negative constraint — so the wall-of-text problem is not actually diagnosed.
assertions: The revised prompt replaces 'helpful assistant' with a specific, domain-named persona
'Don't be too long' is replaced by a checkable numeric limit — a word, sentence, or bullet count
'Try not to miss anything important' is replaced by named sections or fields the summary must contain
At least one negative constraint from the original is restated as an affirmative directive naming what to do rather than what to avoid
The response identifies References as the absent component and says what would fill it, without inventing an example support ticket
The response ends with a short list of what changed and why — in this path the reasoning is part of the deliverable, not padding
The revised prompt is shorter or comparable in instruction count to a version that merely appends rules — it does not fix vagueness by adding more prose
